title: Tunable Superconductivity Mediated by Heavy-Electron Plasmons: Band-Structure and Quantum-Geometric Engineering
abstract: Conventional superconductivity derives its pairing glue from lattice vibrations, tying its characteristic scales to chemistry and atomic masses. Plasmons$-$the collective oscillations of electrons$-$can instead be reshaped through electronic structure engineering, but the principles governing optimal plasmon-mediated pairing remain unclear. Here, we establish such principles for two-carrier systems in which heavy-electron plasmons mediate the pairing of light electrons. Within the random-phase approximation and Eliashberg theory, we calculate the optimal $T_c$ of minimal metallic models and show that it is controlled by a competition between the plasmon energy scale and retardation-driven suppression of the repulsion, yielding optimal carrier densities and band masses. While the plasmon channel alone reaches only $T_c\sim$ 0.1 K, a moderate phonon attraction cooperates with it, boosting $T_c$ by two orders of magnitude to above 20 K. However, the band flattening needed for slow metallic plasmons also favors the development of competing orders. We therefore consider an insulating system in which coherent interband transitions between flat bands generate gapped interband plasmons without free carriers. The heavy-band quantum metric governs the dispersion and electron-plasmon pairing strength of the interband plasmon, while the quantum geometry of the light band suppresses static screening and enhances the net attraction. Because layer separation rapidly weakens pairing, we propose systems with coexisting light and heavy electrons living in different mirror-symmetry sectors of the same layer as promising platforms. Our results establish a new role for flat-band systems in superconductivity: rather than hosting the paired electrons themselves, they can serve as a tunable pairing mediator whose collective charge excitations set the superconducting energy scale beyond their narrow bandwidth.
summary: This work develops a theory for high-temperature superconductivity using plasmons as the pairing glue, moving beyond traditional phonon mechanisms. It introduces the concept of 'flat-band mediators,' where flat bands generate collective excitations that enhance $T_c$ in an adjacent itinerant electron system. The findings suggest promising material platforms like multilayer graphene exhibiting coexisting light and heavy electronic sectors.
main_problem: Establishing fundamental principles for achieving high superconducting critical temperatures ($T_c$) by engineering pairing mechanisms beyond conventional phonon mediation.
main_result: The paper establishes a 'flat-band mediator paradigm,' showing that flat bands can serve as tunable mediators whose collective charge excitations set the superconducting energy scale, potentially boosting $T_c$ significantly above 20 K when combined with phonons.
method: Theoretical calculations utilizing Eliashberg theory and Random Phase Approximation (RPA) to model electron-plasmon interactions in two-carrier and flat-band systems.
model_or_system: The study models two-carrier systems (light/heavy electrons) and insulating systems with flat bands. The pairing mechanism is mediated by plasmons, whose dispersion and coupling are governed by the heavy-electron quantum metric or interband transitions.
key_observables: $T_c$ (critical temperature), Plasmon energy scale ($\Omega_p$), Pairing strength ($\lambda$).
important_parameters: Carrier densities ($n_l, n_h$), effective masses ($m_l, m_h$), quantum geometry parameters ($\zeta$), and phonon coupling constant ($\lambda_{ph}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses the Random Phase Approximation (RPA) and linearized isotropic Eliashberg equations; neglecting vertex corrections beyond Migdal's theorem is a key approximation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic comparisons between phonon-mediated and plasmon-mediated superconductivity, showing $T_c$ dependence on carrier densities, and detailing the quantum geometry effects in flat-band systems.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing general principles (plasmon mediation) to analyzing specific metallic two-carrier models, then advancing to the more complex insulating flat-band scenario, culminating in a platform proposal based on coexisting light/heavy electrons.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity, the reliance on 'quantum geometry' and collective excitations mediated by band structure features (like flat bands) provides theoretical tools applicable to understanding strongly correlated phases driven by geometric constraints or topological effects in quantum materials.
